review_text: I bought this glue to use on my false lashes to give it an eyeliner look for a party event. The lashes felt really glued in, like cement, and when I say CEMENT, they really were. Within 2 1/2 hours I was feeling like the glue was scratching and poking my eyes, it was irritating to my eyes, I couldn’t wait to get home to get them off, but NAY NAY my darlings, no chance in hell, those babies were going to stay glued in for a while, I used makeup remover, wash my face and nothing was going to get these lashes off. Each lash end was loose because I was trying to get them off but stop because my natural lashes were coming out too and it hurt. My eyes were so irritated and red, I was using eye drops to alleviate the pain and discomfort, (thank goodness I work from home and only my husband would be the only to see me… he still has nightmares ‘til this day) this lasted 7+ days, YES 7+ days, a friend of my suggested to go to one of the lash salons near my home and ask for help, (why didn’t I thought of that sooner, don’t know, may God was sending me a message by putting my husband through a test, BTW he is still with me) so I did call a near by salon and they were able to remove the remaining glue attached to the my natural and fake lashes. I gave a 3 star because it did what it said it would, GLUE the false lashes ON, and because DUO is a good brand, I use the glue that drys clear and I have NEVER EVER, had anything like this happened. BUYERS BEWARE, enter to the twilight lash glue zone knowing this can happen to you. I know in part it could have been an allergic reaction to this particular glue, but will never know since I didn’t go and get my eyes checked by a doctor. I do however have scared my husband for life, will need professional help to stop the nightmares, bahahaha!!! All jokes aside, be very careful, although DUO is a good brand, different types of glue have different ingredients to make the glue do it’s thing. Lash on ladies!! :)

review_text: Pros: Nifty brush attachment Silk Epil 7 is a great epilator even without accessories Brush attachment feels fantastic on tired feet If you are prone to ingrown hairs, this might help exfoliate to keep them at bay. YMMV. Silk Epil 7 has a light to show you what you missed. Apparently, with my non-lit epilator, I was missing so much that I'm a bit embarrassed. Cordless (once charged) for your hair removal wanderlust. Massaging rollers on the epilator head really do make it less uncomfortable (they seem to distract nerves just a little) My hair grows in much finer and lighter in color. YMMV. Cons: Brush is only for the body NOT FOR USE ON THE FACE! Brush is not friendly to my sensitive skin Brush pops off too easily during use My advice: If you don't have a Clarisonic brush (with the body brush head), you might like a motorized shower brush. If you really don't care about the brush, you might want to take a look at the other Silk Epil 7 packages out there. Some of them have more or less accessories, and different price points that may be more or less appealing than this Spa package, some have facial hair attachments and some have an electric razor head/accessory. It's up to you. I do recommend the Silk Epil 7 though, but Braun offers enough of a variety of packages that include the Silk Epil 7 that you can get exactly what you need. Lengthier review: The "Spa" Attachment: This is not my first epilator. In fact, this is my second Braun Silk Epil 7 Epilator. My previous one was not part of a "SPA" package. I adore the Silk Epil 7. I used this model before I got the Spa set: [[ASIN:B0077PLNB6 Braun Series 7-7181 Silk Epil Wet & Dry Epilator 1 Count]] I still love the epilator portion and think that the little "headlight" and the bumpy rollers make things more efficient and less uncomfortable (uncomfortable if you have previously epilated or painful if you are a newbie to mechanically ripping the hair out of your legs). The Silk Epil 7 handle is comfortable to hold, it is wet/dry, though I do not like wet epilation (it just doesn't do as thorough a job, for me as doing it dry). I have tried other models from Braun and this one: [[ASIN:B004KMIZK6 Emjoi Optima Corded Epilator]] and at first I thought the Emjoi was the cat's pajamas, but the Silk Epil 7 (and even the 5) is far superior in regards to features, discomfort, and efficiency. I have not even looked at the Emjoi since making the move to the Braun hair rippers. About the brush/spa attachment: The "sonic" brush head dresses up the body of the Silk Epil 7 so it sort of looks like one of those Clarisonic type brushes. At first I was excited that this would replace my Clarisonic and be a space saving and effort saving 2-in-1 extravaganza. Such is not the case. The brush head/attachment for the Silk Epil 7 is strictly for body only and NOT FOR THE FACE. The brush head is good for regular body brushing/exfoliating to help prevent ingrown hairs (something I have never had a problem with since I started using an epilator, but many people do have that problem and an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure). I wanted to use it all over, not just where I used the epilator, and it feels fairly strong and abrasive compared to the more gentle (and quiet!) sounds of my Clarisonic with body brush head. I came out of the shower and was bright pink. My sensitive skin does ok with the Clarisonic, and fine with an exfoliating washcloth but the Silk Epil brush left me bright pink and feeling like I spent the day at the beach. It did, though, make my feet look quite smooth and the sonic vibration and brush were strong enough that my tired feet did feel pampered, though my legs looked about the same. Perhaps other users find the brush more helpful if they use their Silk Epil 7 in the shower. I prefer to epilate dry skin/dry hair, so the only reason I would take it in the shower is to exfoliate the rest of my body, rather than as an adjunct to exfoliation. The brush assembly/attachment was not that friendly as far as being able to angle the whole device to exfoliate my back and the head kept popping off, which was rather annoying and made me think that it is meant more for just the legs (and if just for the legs it seems almost excessive, but some may benefit from the sonic brushing to prevent ingrown hairs- potentially...).

The Silk Epil 7 handle is comfortable to hold, it is wet/dry, though I do not like wet epilation (it just doesn't do as thorough a job, for me as doing it dry). I have tried other models from Braun and this one: [[ASIN:B004KMIZK6 Emjoi Optima Corded Epilator]] and at first I thought the Emjoi was the cat's pajamas, but the Silk Epil 7 (and even the 5) is far superior in regards to features, discomfort, and efficiency. I have not even looked at the Emjoi since making the move to the Braun hair rippers. About the brush/spa attachment: The "sonic" brush head dresses up the body of the Silk Epil 7 so it sort of looks like one of those Clarisonic type brushes. At first I was excited that this would replace my Clarisonic and be a space saving and effort saving 2-in-1 extravaganza. Such is not the case. The brush head/attachment for the Silk Epil 7 is strictly for body only and NOT FOR THE FACE. The brush head is good for regular body brushing/exfoliating to help prevent ingrown hairs (something I have never had a problem with since I started using an epilator, but many people do have that problem and an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure). I wanted to use it all over, not just where I used the epilator, and it feels fairly strong and abrasive compared to the more gentle (and quiet!) sounds of my Clarisonic with body brush head. I came out of the shower and was bright pink. My sensitive skin does ok with the Clarisonic, and fine with an exfoliating washcloth but the Silk Epil brush left me bright pink and feeling like I spent the day at the beach. It did, though, make my feet look quite smooth and the sonic vibration and brush were strong enough that my tired feet did feel pampered, though my legs looked about the same. Perhaps other users find the brush more helpful if they use their Silk Epil 7 in the shower. I prefer to epilate dry skin/dry hair, so the only reason I would take it in the shower is to exfoliate the rest of my body, rather than as an adjunct to exfoliation. The brush assembly/attachment was not that friendly as far as being able to angle the whole device to exfoliate my back and the head kept popping off, which was rather annoying and made me think that it is meant more for just the legs (and if just for the legs it seems almost excessive, but some may benefit from the sonic brushing to prevent ingrown hairs- potentially...).

review_text: I will start out by saying that I did not purchase my Wahl Smart Shaver from Amazon since I found it cheaper elsewhere. With that being said, I'd like to comment based on my usage of this shaver thus far. First of all, I just recently used a Braun 9 series shaver. I literally turned on both shavers, and in my honest opinion, the Wahl was slightly quieter. The Wahl does have some similarities to a Remington shaver. For example, the two inner blades resemble the Remington as does the sound of the shaver. The outter foil seems to be very unique to the Wahl brand. So in using the Wahl Smart Shaver, I found it to be very effective on 2+ days of beard growth as it went through the facial hair with ease. The shaver head is thinner which in my opinion allowed me to get closer than both Braun and Remington shavers. The hypoallergenic foils that have symmetrical and asymmetrical foil slots provided me with an exceptionally close and clean shave. Almost 12 hours after my initial shave, and I barely felt any stubble growth. To me that speaks volumes about this shaver. I was very skeptical about trying this shaver based on the prior reviews here and the fact that the Wahl shaver was cheaper than the leading brands (e.g., Braun, Panasonic, Remington, etc..). However, for now I'm glad I took a chance and decided to give the Wahl Smart Shaver a chance. Also, if you view other sites, this shaver ranks significantly higher than it does amongst Amazon shoppers. Not sure why this is but something doesn't make sense to me. So if you want a clean shave and also don't want to go into debt buying a shaver, I suggest giving this shaver a try. By the way I'm retired military and this would've been nice to use while I was active duty. Lastly, if you're still not convinced, please take into account that Wahl guarantees this shaver for five (5) years. Take a chance. You'll be glad you did!

I would suggest not rinsing the unit itself in water and if in the shower stand away from the showerr water when using. The spinning mechanism that comes up doesn't seem to have a good water seal. review_text: After being scolded by the dentist one-too-many times that I wasn't brushing in circular motions and that I haven't been giving my wisdom teeth enough attention, I recently decided to jump onto the electric toothbrush bandwagon, but at the same time, I had no desire to spend half a truck payment on one with "sonic" cleaning or five-way floss/torture heads. Over the past month, I've found that this Oral-B Vitality, which is actually manufactured by Braun and bears a small Braun logo, cannot be beat for the money! It does just what I need it to, has a nifty compact recharging station with no exposed metal contacts, and my mouth hasn't ever felt cleaner. The only two very minor cons that I think people should be aware of are related to battery life and the two-minute timer. It's probably true that the battery will last 20 minutes between charges, but I've found in daily use that if I don't hang it back on the recharging station after every other use, the bristles spin a bit slower than they do when the battery is fully charged. Not a huge deal, but my time is precious in the morning and I want maximum RPMs, so I prefer not to completely empty the battery beyond the manufacturer's recommendation to do so periodically. Also, I can see the two-minute timer being great for those who have a bad habit of not brushing long enough, but I find personally that I typically brush for about 2-1/2 minutes, even if I'm trying to rush, so it would be nice to have a way to turn the two-minute timer off. The timer isn't a light or a beep, but rather the toothbrush "revs" its engine down and back up a few times once two minutes have elapsed, which makes brushing ineffective over the course of those one to two seconds of revving and thus again wastes precious seconds. Again, not a huge deal, but a way to turn it off would be nice. Otherwise, this toothbrush can't be beat!

Undaria pinnatifida extract is shown to reduce wrinkle depth and improve over-all skin appearance. It also helps to protect the skin's natural stores of collagen and hyaluronic acid. The alteromonas ferment extract is found in deep seawater algae. It has binding properties that help hydration. Salicornia herbacea extract contains good-for-the-skin things – increasing skin barrier and deep hydration. It might even help the skin recover. Arginine protects the skin from free radicals that contribute to fine lines. Arginine in cosmetics hydrates and boosts collagen production. The parfum ingredient is not damaging to the skin. The combination of these ingredients is a friend to the skin's health. Understanding what's in our products ensures that we are buying serums we actually want to put on our faces. But if I wish to carry this deck around, a big book would be cumbersome I suppose. HOWEVER, what is nice about the LWB is they provide a mythical background on the creature, a divinatory meaning, AND magickal use of the card. Nifty! Never have I seen the Magickal Usage option before in a tarot deck. So, card by card, I'm taking in what I think the symbology means then reading the LWB and finding I'm fairly accurate. Either I'm getting better at Tarot or the deck really syncs with me like the Celtic Dragon and Fey decks do (ShapeShifter is a more difficult one for me to grasp now, but I have faith in the future it will become quite the tool for me when I'm ready). Lastly, and one of the reason why I love Lisa Hunt's decks, is the Wands/Air - Swords/Fire connection. Few decks represent that and I've always been more intuitively drawn to that way of thinking, even before my Tradition's teachings reflected the same. If you are a fan of Lisa Hunt -- get this deck. If you are a fan of mythology -- get this deck. If you are a witch or tarot reader who is more connected to the Wands/Air, Swords/Fire -- get this deck. If you are like me and need a reference card now and again (lol) -- get this deck.

review_text: Jung Saem Mool is a famous makeup artist in Korea. You can think of her as like Korea's Bobbi Brown or Laura Mercier. I was really excited to see her products on sale on Amazon. I have dry/combo skin but mostly dry especially in the winter time. I had heard good things about this product but balked at the price. I finally caved when I saw Somi feature it as a guest on a beauty video. Pros: Layerable. It's a thin watery consistency but really does moisturize the skin nicely. This is great to use with other products during very dry or severe weather. It's also great to use to prep dry skin before applying base makeup such as foundation or cushion. Kind of like a watery version of CT's Magic Cream (which is also wonderful to use before applying base makeup). My foundation had never looked so good. Cons: Price. A little does go a long way though; one pump is enough for my whole face. Scent - as other reviewers have mentioned, this is quite heavily scented - it has that typical floral scent found in old-school Korean cosmetics. I sometimes go back and forth about whether I would repurchase. Price makes me hesitate but when I see how nice my foundation looks after, I feel like I need this product! Time will tell....

review_text: For many years I've always straightened my hair because I cannot seem to get the hang of using curling irons to make pretty spiral curls. Wearing the same hairstyle all the time with long hair can get a bit boring so I decided to search on Amazon for styling tools that are easy to use. I initially ordered the [[ASIN:B003FBI9LS Bed Head Deep Waver]] and really loved the results so much that I also purchased this Rock 'n' Roller styling iron, which I affectionately call my "bubble curler." The Bed Head Rock 'n' Roller Ceramic Styling Iron comes with the iron itself along with a black protective glove to protect your hand from the heat of this iron since there is no clamp. The iron measures almost 15 inches in length, with the heating barrel measuring about 5 3/4 inches. The balls measure about one inch in diameter. The cord measures almost six feet so there is plenty of length to move around with it. The iron has a black ball at the top so you can hold it while using it, a safety stand that works well, an on/off switch, a temperature dial that allows you to choose among the low, medium, and high settings as well as the temperatures in between all of them, and a swivel cord so you can easily move the iron around as you use it. I found that it heats up quickly and cools off rapidly as well in case you need to pack it up in your suitcase soon after using it. The glove fits well but I didn't end up using it since it feels a bit awkward to use while trying to grip strands of hair so I took a chance and kept my hand bare, with no problems as long as I styled my hair in front of a mirror so I could watch closely what I was doing. I found this styling iron a bit difficult to use at first but it gets easier with practice. I just winged it and have included some pictures of my end result. There is a chart in the instructions as to what heat setting is most likely appropriate for your hair type but they recommend you start with the lowest setting and increase the heat as needed. I have wavy to medium hair so I started off using the low setting but ended up using the medium setting. I have long hair and it was fairly simple to wrap my hair around the barrel. When I got toward the end of the strands of hair, I carefully wrap them around the barrel, holding my fingers as close as I can to the styling iron without actually touching it. Then I roll the styling iron towards my head as close as I can so my hair gets curled as much as possible. I hold my hair in that position for about 40 seconds and then release it and curl my whole head. It probably took about a half hour to style all of my hair and then I finished by spraying it with hairspray. review_text: Ok, I'll preface this by saying that I've never used any other product to keep a wig on, but I bought this on a recommendation from someone who wears wigs a lot. This does not keep a lace front wig attached to my head AT ALL. It does a very good job of making my real hairs stick to my forehead though. The glue stayed tacky for a very long time. The second time I used it, I waited a good 5 minutes after putting it on my skin before putting the wig on, and it did a better job. However, the wig still slid around a lot, and so I took it off and let the glue dry all the way before putting the wig back on where I wanted it (I had already left home so I couldnt just use the remover). I still dont consider the hold it has to be all that much more securing, and its definitely not worth how uncomfortable it is if you get it in your hair or wig. The remover does an excellent job of taking it all off. Even out of individual hairs, it seems like a little went a long way. Would not recommend for wigs. I'm not sure what its other uses are, but dont buy it if you're hoping to use it to keep a wig in place.

review_text: I like to fashion myself as sort of a cologne connoisseur…….a man’s man who just really likes to smell good all the time. I began wearing cologne shortly after I started my first job in high school, and ever since then I have been enamored with finding great smelling colognes. When I saw this cologne, and I read what it was inspired by, I felt that it was almost a must have for me. The first and most obvious reason most of us on here purchased this cologne is because it is inspired by Ralph Lauren Polo Red; and since that cologne is fairly pricey, undoubtedly most of us felt they were going to get a sweet deal. Now, you may ask what is the difference between this and the legitimate cologne that you would pay 60$ or more for? The first thing to know is that this cologne does not smell exactly like Polo Red at all. In fact, it is very loosely inspired by the actual scent. I challenge anyone to buy and smell the original cologne, then buy and smell this and tell me it’s exactly the same thing. Sorry folks, this just isn’t the same smell. It does, however, share similarities with the Polo Red…..which makes it enticing, but it just is not the same thing. The main issue that I have with this cologne is that it simply does not last more than an hour at best. I now understand why you get a 3.0-ounce bottle for 15$, and that is because you are constantly reapplying it to keep the smell fresh. With a normal (and quality) cologne I can go pretty much the extent of my eight-hour shift at work and still smell relatively fresh, but this cologne honestly started fading at about 20-30 minutes after application. In the end this may not bother folks who just want something cheap to make them smell good for a little while. Heck, even I like the way it smells at first. The problem for those of us who fashion ourselves fragrance snobs is that the scent just fades away too quickly. If affordability is what you look for in a cologne, then by all means this is your product. I, however, would just suggest spending the extra couple of bucks and buying the real deal. I can’t see how anyone would be disappointed with that at all.

review_text: I've been using electric shavers of one form or another for over fifty years, and this one I rate as the best yet. First it's one of the most comfortable. I can comfortably shave the back of my neck with this shaver where others irritated. Second, it's by far the fastest shaver yet, plus it gets any long hairs in its path. I attribute at least part of its speed to the third row of cutters which sets this one apart from many others. Third, it works fine wet, lotion or water, or dry. I'm using up some of the lotion cartridges from a previous Norelco dispensing shaver and it works very smoothly with them. Fourth, it went well over a month on the initial charge. Fifth, the built in trimmer is effective and convenient as opposed to some trimmers I've had that had to be attached in place of the shaving head. And finally it's easy to clean and packs light and compact for traveling. The battery level meter is nice for checking when the charge is full. When the battery does finally give up and you're in the middle of a shave the charging cord can be used directly into the shaver to finish, then when ready for charging it can be connected to the charging stand for a regular charge. Charging is done relatively fast also, in roughly about an hour or so it's full and ready to go another month or longer. There's often the argument between basic types of shavers, foil or rotary being two of the subjects. I recently tried one of the newer and recommended foil shavers and it's now on the shelf. Foil shavers for me miss too much, long hairs for sure, but they are not as effective on the regular stubble for me as a rotary shaver. That would be bad enough but my experience with foil shavers was if you missed a place in the previous shave, you won't get it next time either even though you go over it. I often had to use the trimmers on foil shavers, even the best of them, for just regular shaving chores. I've bought and used a lot of electric shavers, but I've never had one this good before of any brand.

review_text: This certainly does lessen pain. I have spent a great deal of time and money on damaged vertebrae in my neck. Doctors, MRIs, xrays, physical therapy and special pillows enabled me to turn my head enough to drive, but the pain was still there and very sharp. Only 50% success was predicted with surgery so I declined. At my gym are many equestrians, and they told me they used the same DMSO on their hands and sore muscles that they used for their horses and got from their vets. They all said they had used it for years (for themselves as well as for their horses) without problems. They did say it is important to wash hands after using to avoid problems getting it in eyes, nose, etc. I don't have a horse or a horse vet. But I looked on the Internet and discovered what I was told was true, and Amazon sold human versions of DMSO. This was my second order of DMSO cream. A friend swiped mine after he tried it and it stopped the pain from the torn miniscus in his knee. Yes, a man. A man with a bad knee who needs to earn his living pressure cleaning, painting houses, crawling under sinks for plumbing, etc. He did not care that it smelled like Roses, only that it worked and would help him on the job. As a female, I like the Roses but the fragrance doesn't last long anyway. Every morning after my shower I massage the cream into my neck tendons and vertebrae. Then I wash my hands and continue with my morning routine. By the time I am ready to dress, the cream has absorbed and most pain is gone. I try to apply more cream at night, giving it time to absorb before crawling into bed. Although this is a topical (surface) application, it seems to have a lasting effect - if I forget it at night there still seems to be less pain in the morning than I used to experience. The jar will last a long time. You only want enough to enable massaging it into the joints or muscles. Too much and you will just have to wipe it off before dressing.

review_text: This is a review for all three of the moisturizers. Green Tea - This mask is for people who deal with excess sebum. That being said, I use this one the most. Not only does my skin feel hydrated instead of greasy in the morning, but after the third use I noticed less breakouts around my chin and jawline (I have hormonal acne and horribly sensitive skin). Black Tea : This mask improves elasticity of the skin. I haven't used this long enough to notice a huge difference, but my skin does feel plump when I wake up, and my mom has had the same result! Strawberry - Like most strawberry skin care products, this one is for people who deal with dry skin. I won't need to use this until the cold seasons arrive, but my mom needs heavy moisturizing products year-round. Her skin has definitely been looking more hydrated and brighter! Instructions and ingredients are provided on the boxes, both in Korean and English. I only have two small complaints about the products: 1. There's a very noticeable amount of fragrance. They all smell great, but it's a bit strong. Thankfully, the smell does fade after the moisturizer is massaged into the skin. My face normally can't tolerate products with so much fragrance, but so far all has gone well. 2. The packaging. Yes, it is adorable, but I'd prefer the spoon be able to stay in the cup. You use the spoon to scoop out the tapioca pearls and smash them up in your palm. It's a long spoon, and it pulls out a lot of moisturizer with it. With this product a little goes a long way (which makes it a total steal at it's current price), so I scrape off a lot of excess. Like I said, those are small complaints, so this product is very much worth trying out. So long as Etude House keeps making it I'll keep buying it.

review_text: These are very thick which is great. Generally KISS brand is all I buy because they withstand a whole lot of cleaning and abuse lol my parrot did take a chunk out of one of the nails but hey, that beak is a force of nature. I first lay out all the nails I’m going to use then begin application. Cover your natural nail with a good coat of glue then put some on the fake nail. review_text: I have this mat, the Bundle Monster mat, and the Ejiubas mat, and this one wins first place in terms of overall quality! It drives me crazy that it doesn't have any black areas for stamping & whatnot (thus, the deduction of one star), but its value, its reasonably sized nail guides, and best of all, the softness of the silicone makes this one the superior choice in my opinion. DESIGN In terms of design, I believe the other two mats are superior over Uber Chic, although UC's isn't bad. Bundle Monster's Lotus Mat is my favorite, but I'm also partial to lotus flowers ;) Its nail guides are ridiculously large, though, but it *does* have black sections to practice on, so that's a huge plus. The Ejiubas mat has a pretty cool & very unique layout compared to all other mats, with its nail sizing grids in both black and white, while still leaving plenty of empty space to work on. One thing I do love about the UC mat is the amount of empty space it features. Some mats out there that I haven't mentioned here are SO busy with verbiage & useless "features" that it's a huge turn off. Less is definitely more! VALUE With regard to value, Ejiubas wins, hands down. I purchased mine for $13, and it came with a great little carry bag! Bundle Monster loses miserably in this category. And, Uber Chic falls somewhere in the middle, which makes its value "okay" in my opinion. TEXTURE - THE DEAL-BREAKER! The (negative) deal-breaker for me is the stickiness of the other two mats. And as a disclaimer, I'm using the word "sticky," although it's not literally sticky... Rubbery is probably a better word, but I'm going with sticky ;) So, I can't stand how *everything* sticks to the Ejiubas mat to the point that you can't even blow or fan debris off of it with your hand. This means it always feels like it needs to be cleaned, it's difficult to keep clean, and actually cleaning it is kind-of a pain. The Bundle Monster mat falls somewhere between Ejiubas and Uber Chic in terms of stickiness. It's much better than the Ejiubas mat, but still sticky enough to be plenty annoying. The Uber Chic mat, though? It's heavenly smooth :) I love it! It's very soft, and very easy to keep clean. Absolutely zero complaints on that front. CONCLUSION If Uber Chic would add some black stamping sections, this mat would be absolutely flawless in my opinion. Every mat out there seems to have at least one superior and one inferior feature that makes it difficult to choose the "best" one. If it were up to me, I'd use the Uber Chic mat with the Bundle Monster design, except with Uber Chic's nail guide sizes, and Ejiubas' price point & free carry bag. Maybe I'll just have to make one of these, so I can finally have the perfect silicone nail art mat! ;)

review_text: It does smell like an orange creamsicle in the best way (yummy!), but if I get a big direct sniff of my hand right after putting it on, it does have the smell reminiscent of eating a really good tangy, fresh apricot, too. Even some lotions that advertise “natural fragrance,” I have sensitivity to, but this one is no problem! No sneezing, wheezing, or headaches from it. It’s a delicious smell, but not too strong or overpowering, and not fake smelling. The scent subsides quickly after a short bit of time passes, but is still there if you sniff the skin directly. I’ve tried their lavender & lemon coconut (both tend to be favorite scents/scent combos for me when done naturally), and those are nice, but this is my favorite one, unexpectedly. I normally make my own really moisture intensive thick creams & lotion bars (with beeswax, cocoa butter, shea butter & olive oil.) These I usually apply to my hands every time I wash, because my skin dries out so easily. It keeps cracked hands at bay. This lotion is not a replacement for intensive creams like that. But this lotion is lovely when I want something that *doesn’t leave my hands feeling greasy*, applies easily, soaks in nicely, & smells good. It’s kinda my “treat myself” lotion. I can also put it out for guests who are used to more traditional lotion consistency, and have them like it, while not being a problem for my breathing. It works great to include in a gift basket, too. I can’t say this will work for every person with scent sensitivities (and don’t assume it’s okay if someone’s told you no scents...some people have dangerous health reactions to even natural fragrances, among other possible serious concerns that need to be respected), but it is definitely one worth looking into if you are the one with sensitivities, trying to find scents you are okay with. It is 1000 x better than most of the lotions with synthetic fragrances, and even some of the stronger ones that claim natural fragrance.

I would definitely recommend this product!!!

review_text: Update: The top pair in the 234 was my favorite because it's the most natural looking but after 2 uses, one of the magnets fell off! This brand has quality issues. I decided to order many other brands of magnetic lashes (Newcally, LAMIX, Coolours) and I found that the magnets for the Yiwamica's lashes are considerably weaker. The other brands lashes would pop on and when pulled off would pull my skin a little. This brand's magnets do not do that. I have to press the eyelashes on and then corners would dislodge. I thought it was due to the liner but no, it's the magnets! Between the magnets falling off completely and the weak magnets, I'm downgrading from 4 to 2 stars. As for the styles, I bought 3 sets from this listing: 230, 231, and 234. See my photo. The 234 is a set of 3 with a natural pair, a denser natural pair same length, and a longest natural pair. The length difference is probably 1mm, very hard to tell on the tray (I didn’t measure with ruler or anything) but you can tell in person when wearing them. I think only the first pair looks truly natural on me for everyday use because I have small Asian hooded eyes. The other two in the 234 tray are sort of natural but I would not use them for day time use. The 231 has 2 pairs that looked the same as the longest pair in the 234 set...again not natural enough for small eyes for day time use. The 230 has crisscrossed lashes where it is longer towards the outer corners and shorter towards the inner. These lashes are longer than those in the 231 and 234. I ended up returning 231 because it was a repeat of my least favorite pair in the 234 set. The 230 box had quality issues. One of the lash strands was super long on one of the lashes. The 230 set was also glued to the plastic holder instead of magnetized to strips on the tray like the other two sets. When I removed the lashes from the holder, the middle magnet fell off 2 of the lashes! I also got a eyeliner and 2 lash pair set from the same company. You can see in my photo. That eye liner turned out to be really bad so I returned that. Instead, I use the Aroama brand of magnetic liner also sold on Amazon (the one with over 1,000 reviews) with these lashes. The magnetics in these lashes are sorta big but since I have to draw the liner really thick for them to stay at all, it’s tough to even notice the magnets. The thick liner could also contribute to the lashes not looking as natural. I want to mention the magnet spacing is inconsistent across this brand. There are always 5 magnets but some are gapped evenly while others you get 2 magnets on each end and one in the middle with a huge gap on each side. The ends of the lashes do tend to detach from the eye easily for me as compared to the middle so the configuration with 2 magnets on the ends helps me. The spacing is purely up to your preference though. Pay attention to the product photos to see which magnet spacing you would get.

As for the styles, I bought 3 sets from this listing: 230, 231, and 234. See my photo. The 234 is a set of 3 with a natural pair, a denser natural pair same length, and a longest natural pair. The other two in the 234 tray are sort of natural but I would not use them for day time use. The 231 has 2 pairs that looked the same as the longest pair in the 234 set...again not natural enough for small eyes for day time use. The 230 has crisscrossed lashes where it is longer towards the outer corners and shorter towards the inner. These lashes are longer than those in the 231 and 234. I ended up returning 231 because it was a repeat of my least favorite pair in the 234 set. The 230 box had quality issues. One of the lash strands was super long on one of the lashes. The magnetics in these lashes are sorta big but since I have to draw the liner really thick for them to stay at all, it’s tough to even notice the magnets. There are always 5 magnets but some are gapped evenly while others you get 2 magnets on each end and one in the middle with a huge gap on each side. The ends of the lashes do tend to detach from the eye easily for me as compared to the middle so the configuration with 2 magnets on the ends helps me. review_text: Woolzies has outdone themselves yet again with their 100% Sweet Almond Oil!! I can not say an adequate number of glorious things about this stuff!I use it for everything ranging from homemade face scrub, shampoo, and moisturizer… to body mist, massage oil, lip balm, and shaving cream!! When I make smoothies with a great deal of vitamin K (such as kale) or pro-vitamin A (such as carrots or apricots) the sweet almond oil (Excellent Source of MUFAs) improves the absorption of these fat-soluble nutrients into my body! It also contains a truckload of vitamin E (Antioxidant) which aids in boosting the immune system, supports a healthy inflammatory response and benefits as a cicatrizant, “ A medicine or application that promotes the healing of a sore or wound, or the formation of a cicatrix. [1913 Webster]” So yeah… this stuff is truly badass! BEST PART... this particular sweet almond oil is extremely mellow in fragrance and flavor. In fact, if I were not the one blending together the ingredients I would be oblivious to its existence in the mix. In any case…I read a review that claimed the scent or flavor of this oil was not the finest, which perhaps could be the ‘pseudo truth’ IF someone was expecting an intensely rich almond essence. (This is what would be found in bitter almond oil. Actually known as almond essential oil) Nevertheless, the ‘aroma/flavor’ or better yet, the lack there of, contained within this particular oil is precisely what I look for when I purchase a product that can be incorporated into my diet or included in so many personal products. My intent is such that I can exercise full control over the fragrance or flavor of my creations. Typically I do so by mixing in some of my favorite essential oils, dried herbs or citrus zests. In sum, I’ve tolerated many but valued only a few products as much as I do this oil. It has earned its place among my officially declared ‘household staple items’! For its versatility, benefits and purity Woolzies 100% Pure Sweet Almond Oil has officially won me over!

review_text: NOTE - It says this is for gel nail polish, glitter gel, dip powder, or nail glue. It is NOT FOR ACRYLIC NAILS OR POLY GEL! I do a lot gel polish and a lot of dip powder on my nails, so I always have to use acetone to remove the polish/dip powder. When I saw this was a gel polish remover kit that had a NON-acetone polish remover, I was really intrigued! I was even more intrigued when it said it “gently removes gel nail polish, glitter gel, dip powder, or nail glue from your nails without damaging within 5 mins, the gel polish remover even can remove the toughest polish quickly and effectively, recovering the original state of nature!” To say it removes gel polish and dip powder gently within 5 minutes is a HUGE claim for a NON-acetone polish remover. To say that it also removes glitter gel gently within 5 minutes is an ever BIGGER claim for a NON-acetone polish remover! Even when I use my 100% acetone to remove dip powder and glitter polish, it takes longer than 5 minutes! So, for this to be NON-acetone but say I removes gel polish, gel glitter, and dip powder gently within 5 minutes…I had to try it! Then, I got the product…It comes in a nice outer product box that is sealed with plastic wrapping around it. It is made in China. It does have an ingredient list, which is really short…”Alcohol, Acetone, Propylene Glycol, Essence, Deionized Water.” Yep, you see that right, ingredient #2 is….ACETONE! Exactly what they said this did NOT have in it! They are calling it a NON-acetone gel nail polish remover, yet the second ingredient is ACETONE!! After that I realized, the product name itself didn’t even say it was a NON-acetone polish remover. It was only in the product description that they said it didn’t have acetone in it. It said, “NON-ACETONE GEL NAIL POLISH REMOVER KIT: The gel nail polish remover, acetone-free remover liquid, is infused with premium formula.” Just a straight up LIE! 🤦‍♀️ On top of that, they’re all over the place on how long you’re supposed to let this sit in your nails. First, they say quite a few times that it removes the product “within 5 minutes.” But, then in the product description when they get to the part of how to use it, they say “wait 5-8 minutes.” THEN, if you look at the product photos, the 6th photo has steps of how to use it. There it says to wait “8-10 minutes.” They just can’t decide! Normally, to remove my gel polish or dip powder, I would first file each nail a little to kind of break the seal. Then, I would take a little cotton round, dip it on my 100% acetone to soak it, place that on my nail, place a soak-off clip over it to hold it in place, and let it sit for about 15-20 minutes before it would even start to come off! If it’s glitter polish or glitter dip nail powder, it needs to sit even longer sometimes! So, for this gel polish remover to be NON-acetone and say it works within 5 minutes, I was really excited to see that! Of course, imagine my disappointment when I get it and see the ingredients on the back Includes ACETONE as the second ingredient in this “NON-acetone gel polish remover.” For use, it says to apply the polish remover to a cotton pad, put the cotton pad on the nail, clip it on with the soak-off clip, and then wait for 5-8 minutes, then remove it. I thought it was funny how it said it removes the product “within 5 minutes” quite a few times in the bullet points prior to the part where it tells you how to use the gel polish remover, but then when it gets to the part where it tells you how to use it, it says to “wait 5-8 minutes.” So, that means it works within 8 minutes. Saying it works “within 5 minutes” means that it will remove the product in 5 minutes or less. They should have said within 8 minutes if you’re supposed to wait 5-8 minutes. BUT, THEN, if you look at the product photos, there is one that shows the steps for how to use the gel polish remover. It’s the last photo before the video (6th photo). It says first file the nail surface. Second, soak the cotton pads in the nail remover. Third, cover nails with cotton pad folded in half. Fourth, and this is the important part, fix the nails with the nail clips and then remove the clips and pads “after 8-10 minutes.” Fifth, use the cuticle pusher to remove all the popped off polish.” So, first, they repeatedly said that this gel polish remover would remove product “within 5 minutes.” Then, it changed to “wait 5-8 minutes.” But, then, it says “8-10 minutes.” So, definitely seems to be some confusion there with what they wanted to put. Of course, removing the product “within 5 minutes” sounds a lot better than 5-8 minutes and waaaay better than 8-10 minutes. But, I’d rather a company just say what it is than try to sell it to me using some random numbers. But, even if it takes 10 minutes, it’s still faster than it takes when I use 100% acetone, so I was still really interested to see how this would work! Again, imagine my surprise when I got it and saw the second ingredient listed for this “NON-acetone gel polish remover” is ACETONE!! I liked how they included a little bottle to put the polish remover in and cotton pads, so you just need to put the cotton pad on the top and push down to get the remover onto the pad. It also includes 10 soak-off clips to use. It also includes a cuticle pusher, which can be used to scrape the polish off once it is ready, and a nail file. So, it includes everything you need to remove your gel polish/dip powder! Even though they totally lied about it being a NON-acetone polish remover, since I usually use 100% acetone on my nails, I figured I’d give it a try anyways. And another thing..since it has acetone in it, it has a STRONG odor like acetone nail polish remover have, which I also thought was funny because on the product page, if you scroll down to “Customer Questions & Answers,” someone asked if it had a strong smell. The SELLER responded with, “No, it does not. It is colourless and low odour.” Along with a strong odor, it isn’t colorless - it has a slight yellow kind of tint to it. Looking at the other questions and answers I saw someone else asked if the kit came with cotton pads and the SELLER answered, “Yes, I get cotton pads with my purchase.” What?! “With YOUR purchase,” you’re the seller! 🤦‍♀️ 😂 Just ridiculous all around… As for the products in the kit… The nail polish remover works just like nail polish removers work. It isn’t as strong as 100% acetone. It definitely takes longer to remove my gel polish and dip powders, especially the glitter polishes. It takes longer than the 15-20 minutes it takes with my 100% acetone. No where near the 5-10 minutes the product page says. It doesn’t even work better than my Sally Nail Polish remover, which has acetone as the 1st ingredient. It does work better than any of my ACTUALLY non-acetone nail polish removers, which won’t remove my gel polish or dip powders (or at least I’m not patient enough to wait to see how long it would take for them to remove it 😂). The clips work just like any other plastic soak-off clips I’ve used before. The cotton pads are little square pads that are stiff at first, but soften once the nail polish remover is applied. They work just like any other pads I’ve gotten before. The little nail polish remover push dispenser bottle works okay. It takes quite a few pumps to get any nail polish remover to come out, but it comes out eventually. I’m interested to see if the bottle holds up with the nail polish remover inside it given that there is acetone in it. I’ve had bottles like these before, kind of plastic type feeling bottles, and the acetone usually eats away at it and I have to remove it before it starts leaking. So, maybe this is made out of something that can handle it. Or, maybe since this isn’t 100% acetone, maybe it’ll handle it okay. But, I’ll be keeping my eye on it since the 2nd ingredient is acetone. Overall, I’d say, if you’re looking for a kit that has all this in it - soak-off clips, nail file, cuticle pusher, cotton pads, nail polish remover push dispenser bottle, and nail polish with acetone in it, this is a good kit. The price isn’t too bad given what you get and how large of a bottle of nail polish remover you get. But, if you’re looking for a NON-acetone nail polish remover - This is NOT it! This has acetone has the 2nd ingredient, so you’ll need to look elsewhere. If you’re looking for nail polish remover that is 100% acetone, this isn’t it. If you’re looking for nail polish remover that works quickly in 5-10 minutes like the product page says, this isn’t it. If you’re looking to buy from a brand that is honest in their description, this isn’t it. So, basically, I’d say, if you’re looking for a nail polish remover with acetone in it, that works like any other nail polish remover that has acetone in it but isn’t 100% acetone and that comes with everything else in this kit, then I’d say go for it. Otherwise, I’d look elsewhere. I’m giving this 2 stars because of all the lies on the product page!

review_text: There are only a few reviews on Castle Forbes' Special Reserve Neroli. A couple are on here, a few randomly online. You have to dig for them. So if you're reading this, you're more of a fragrance lover than the average Tommy Bahama fan. Put simply, CF Neroli is not a popular EDP, nor is the brand. You have to know some things about fragrance and have a specific knowledge about neroli itself, to have come searching for Castle Forbes version. This is how I came to know this brand and EDP myself. My view is that it's not worth the cost of 160USD. That's a lot of money for a 3.4oz. bottle. CF has a nice brand image, the EDP presentation is great, and the quality of the materials used are outstanding. However, the scent alone falls short. Neroli Reserve starts out wonderfully: crisp orange and neroli, combined with greens like pine, grass and hedges. You feel like you're at the beach, sitting just where the sand dunes meet a lush forest. This lasts for about 20 minutes. Then the "woody/musky" basenotes kick in, and this is where CF got it wrong. It deteriorates into a powdery, barbershop, very British scent. It's something your grandmother (not grandfather) would have worn if she lived in London in 1865. Designer houses today try and replicate this a bit, usually just producing a floraly, loud, baby powder vibe (see MDCI Invasion Barbare). This basenote scent is what then dominates for the next 10 hours, more if you've sprayed any arm/chest hair. The woods aren't masculine woods, just faint tree bark really. The EDP strength is phenomenal; this stuff lasts. The only problem is whether or not you like to smell like a woman, particularly a powderpuff with flowers. I do get some faint whiffs of neroli, but it's overpowered by the floral powder. I would not recommend this for a man, and unfortunately, would recommend Tom Ford's Neroli Portofino over this. A different vibe for sure (more aquatic), but TF's neroli sustains. Overall, 3 of 5 stars just because the ingredients are so good, but the scent isn't as much neroli as it is the musky amber that CF used. Bummer.

review_text: I'm in my late-20s and was looking to start a preventative care/anti-wrinkle regimen. I'm not very wrinkly yet... but have noticed some slight crepe-yness/very fine lines under my eyes, possibly from inserting/removing my contacts everyday and stretching my eyes out. I've also noticed some slight lines forming on my left forehead, and some frown/smile lines around my mouth/chin which I'd like to prevent from becoming more noticeable. I have an oily T-zone (forehead, nose, chin) which is prone to breakouts so I normally do not apply any moisturizer to these areas of my face. But this cream has different ingredients than my usual average face lotions so I decided to give it a go, and applied this cream even to the oily zones of my face. It did not cause me to break out, and did not increase how greasy these areas became throughout the day. I've been using this cream 2x/daily for a little less than a month now and I actually think it helped improve the condition of my skin in these problem areas. My forehead and chin have slightly fewer breakouts, and just seem smoother in appearance (tone, color, less random blotchiness). The fine lines under my eyes are still there, but do seem to diminish whenever I apply this cream--it seems to fill in the lines temporarily and the cream moisturizes the dry skin so it looks smoother and is less visible. This moisturizer has a great non-greasy texture. It comes out feeling just rich & creamy enough, and then my skin just drinks it all up, feeling soft, light, and moisturized. It barely has a smell at all, and the tiny bit of fragrance fades almost immediately. Overall, I do like this face cream since I have noticed a slight improvement in my skin in less than 1 month. I wouldn't consider it a MIRACLE cream since I have had experiences with very expensive (out of my usual budget-type expensive) creams/serums that DID deliver more noticeable results. But for this price point, and the slight results I have noticed, I would recommend this to someone with similar skin problems as me. And I would also consider buying this again.

review_text: First of all, a lot of people have said this is useless or that it doesn't work. That isn't remotely true. Versions of this device, in one form or another, have been on the market for like 50 years because they DO work. However, the device has an incredibly steep learning curve, is not intuitive to use, has multiple design problems, and costs way more than it should. One of the frustrating aspects of this device is that all of the probes/needles have a spring base. This is there to prevent an inexperienced user (read basically everyone who buys one of these) from accidentally applying current to a part of their skin other than a follicle and thereby potentially causing skin damage. This is an admirable idea, but in practice it means that unless you are 1,000% on-target with the probe, it will just just constantly bounce around on your skin without going into the follicle, truly a frustrating experience! The probes/needles are also far more expensive than professional electrolysis needles, likely due to the silly spring mechanism. I'll note that there are numerous guides for modifying this device (search Inverness OneTouch modifications if curious) to use pro needles which increases its utility and ease of use but also makes it potentially more dangerous if you don't know what you're doing. Now for the good, this device gives you the ability to perform safe, effective, truly permanent hair removal on yourself and/or your loved ones in the comfort of your own home and at your own pace, accounting for your own comfort level. "Professional" electrologists are all over the place in terms of effectiveness, quality, value, actual, literal professionalism, etc. My experience with them has been uniformly poor despite patronizing nearly a dozen at this point. This is cheaper, more convenient, and, assuming you know what you're doing, more likely to be effective on a permanent basis than professional treatment, especially if the electrologist in question is not a 100% galvanic operator (this device is an unsophisticated example of a 100% galvanic machine). Just wish it were a little bit less frustrating to use!
